topic: Gradient descent and optimisation for second-year mechanical engineering undergraduates

entry_point.discipline_context: Mechanical engineers often seek the configuration that minimises stored energy while satisfying constraints.
entry_point.rationale: Starting from a familiar mechanical picture makes the optimisation problem concrete before introducing gradients and updates.
entry_point.analogy_boundary: The mechanical analogy is useful for intuition, but the optimisation formulation is broader and does not assume a physical force field.

chapter_sequence.title: From potential energy to optimisation
chapter_sequence.purpose: Introduce the optimisation problem through potential energy, equilibrium, and stationarity.

chapter_sequence.title: Smoothness, convexity, and the shape of the energy landscape
chapter_sequence.purpose: Explain why smoothness and convexity matter for reliable descent and stable equilibrium.

chapter_sequence.title: Gradient descent as numerical relaxation
chapter_sequence.purpose: Present the update rule, explain step-size selection, and connect the mathematics to executable Python.

chapter_sequence.title: Convergence behaviour and step-size choices
chapter_sequence.purpose: Compare the general convex rate with the stronger linear rate for strongly convex problems.

chapter_sequence.title: Momentum, stochastic updates, and second-order ideas
chapter_sequence.purpose: Introduce practical extensions and the role of curvature in optimisation.

implementation_strategy: Use a simple one-dimensional Python example to show the gradient-descent update directly and keep the code readable for second-year students.
assessment_strategy: Include a short set of exercises that test stationarity, step-size intuition, and the link between the update rule and the mechanical analogy.
